legal_sources.applicability: Entry rules include advance-notice, emergency, requested-service and prospective-tenant-showing exceptions. Do not omit the exceptions.

legal_sources.article: Sec. 12.5-16. Remedies for abuse of access rights.
legal_sources.text:
(a)
If the tenant refuses to allow lawful access, the landlord may obtain injunctive relief
to compel access or terminate the rental agreement. In either case, the landlord may
recover damages and reasonable attorney's fees.
(b)
If the landlord makes an unlawful entry or a lawful entry in an unreasonable manner
the tenant may obtain injunctive relief to prevent the recurrence of the conduct and
recover an amount equal to not more than two (2) months' rent or the damages sustained,
whichever is greater, and reasonable attorney's fees.
(c)
If the landlord makes a lawful entry to make alterations or improvements that materially
interfere with the tenant's use of the premises or if the landlord makes repeated
demands for entry otherwise lawful, but which have the effect of harassing the tenant
after being notified in writing by the tenant that tenant feels harassed by such repeated
demands, the tenant may obtain injunctive relief to prevent the recurrence of the
conduct, or terminate the rental agreement. In each case, the tenant may recover an
amount equal to not more than two (2) months' rent or the damages sustained, whichever
is greater, and reasonable attorney's fees. The provisions of this section shall not
apply to alterations or improvements done by the landlord to correct cited housing
code violations, except in the cases of the landlord's unreasonableness, neglect,
or negligence in correcting the violations.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

legal_sources.text:
(a)
The landlord shall maintain the premises in compliance with all applicable housing
codes of the city and shall promptly make any and all necessary repairs to fulfill
that obligation, provided, however, that the tenant may knowingly and intentionally
elect and agree to repair the premises to bring them into conformity with the applicable
housing codes of the city. The burden shall be on the landlord to establish a knowing
and intentional election on the part of the tenant to repair the premises in compliance
with the applicable housing code. A mere recital in a form lease that tenant has covenanted
to repair will not be sufficient, it being the intention of this article that any
agreement with the tenant to repair be bargained for in fact. A separate hand-written
paragraph in the lease showing:
(1)
That the tenant has been informed of this article and the existing code violations;
(2)
That he/she has affirmatively elected and bargained to repair the violations listed
and other items listed; and
(3)
The inducement for such arrangements, will be prima facie evidence that such provision
was entered into in good faith and was bargained for in fact.
(b)
Nothing in this article shall be interpreted so as to restrict the authority of city
inspectors to cite a landlord for violation of building code provisions.
(c)
Before a tenant initially enters into or renews a rental agreement for a rental unit,
the landlord or any person authorized to enter into a rental agreement on the landlord's
behalf shall disclose to the tenant in writing any housing code violations which have
been cited by the building official and which remain uncorrected for that rental unit
and the common area of the premises.
(d)
This article shall not be interpreted as decreasing or diminishing the implied warranty
of habitability as adopted by the Illinois Supreme Court.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

legal_sources.applicability: Subject to Secs. 12.5-2 and 12.5-7. A tenant repair election must be knowing, intentional and actually bargained for, with the burden on the landlord; a form-lease recital alone is insufficient. The described separate handwritten paragraph is prima facie evidence, not stated as the sole permissible form of proof. Distinguish payment allocation from an agreement to perform code-compliance repairs, and verify the particular repair and bargaining facts.

legal_sources.text:
(a)
A landlord who receives a security deposit of one hundred dollars ($100.00) or more
from a tenant to secure the payment of rent or to compensate for damage to property
shall pay interest to the tenant, computed from the date the deposit is paid, at a
rate equal to the interest paid by the largest commercial bank, as measured by total
assets, having its main banking premises in Champaign County, Illinois, on minimum
deposit passbook savings accounts as of the thirtieth of June immediately preceding
the inception of the rental agreement on any such deposit held by the landlord for
more than six (6) months.
(b)
The landlord shall, within thirty (30) days after the end of each twelve-month rental
period, pay to the tenant any interest, by cash or credit to be applied to rent due,
except when the tenant is in default under the terms of the lease. For the purposes
of this provision, default shall mean nonpayment of rent or a successful claim by
the landlord for possession of the premises for good cause other than nonpayment of
rent. A landlord who willfully fails or refuses to pay the interest required by this
article shall, upon a finding by a circuit court that he/she has willfully failed
or refused to pay, be liable for an amount equal to the amount of the security deposit,
together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

legal_sources.text:
(a)
A lessor of residential real property who has received a security deposit from a lessee
to secure the payment of rent or to compensate for damage to the leased property may
not withhold any part of that deposit as compensation for property damage unless he
or she has, within thirty (30) days of the date that the lessee vacated the premises,
furnished to the lessee, delivered in person or by mail directed to his or her last
known address, an itemized statement of the damage allegedly caused to the premises
and the estimated or actual cost for repairing or replacing each item on that statement,
attaching the paid receipts, or copies thereof, for the repair or replacement. If
the lessor utilizes his or her own labor to repair any damage caused by the lessee,
the lessor may include the reasonable cost of his or her labor to repair such damage.
If estimated cost is given, the lessor shall furnish the lessee with paid receipts,
or copies thereof, within thirty (30) days from the date the statement showing estimated
cost was furnished to the lessee, as required by this section. If no such statement
and receipts, or copies thereof, are furnished to the lessee as required by this section,
the lessor shall return the security deposit in full within forty-five (45) days of
the date that the lessee vacated the premises.
(b)
Upon a finding by a circuit court that the landlord has refused to supply the itemized
statement required herein, or has supplied such statement in bad faith, and has failed
or refused to return the amount of the security deposit due within the time limits
provided, the landlord shall be liable for an amount equal to twice the amount of
the security deposit due, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
(c)
Reserved.
(d)
The decorating of the rental unit after the tenant vacates, including painting and
carpet cleaning, unless walls or carpets are damaged beyond normal wear, shall not
be considered as damage and the costs thereof shall not be charged to the security
deposit.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94; Ord. No. 2000-07-066, 7-17-00)

legal_sources.article: Sec. 12.5-23. Tenant remedies for landlord's failure to maintain.
legal_sources.text:
(a)
If the landlord fails to disclose to the tenant in writing any cited housing code
violations as required in this article, or to correct any condition constituting a
subsequently cited housing code violation within the time specified in a duly served
notice to correct such cited housing code violation by the building official, the
tenant affected by the condition may notify the landlord in writing of the tenant's
intention to correct the condition at the landlord's expense. If the landlord, after
receipt of such notice by the tenant, fails to correct the condition within the time
specified for the performance of any act required by the notice of the building official
or any duly granted extension thereof, the tenant, after first obtaining a contractor's
firm certificate of insurance from the qualified appropriate tradesman who is to perform
the work, and after furnishing such certificate to the landlord in the case of any
work to be done on the premises, may have the work done in a competent manner and,
after submitting to the landlord a paid itemized invoice and, where applicable, a
properly completed waiver of lien, may deduct from his or her rent the amount thereof.
(b)
If the cited housing code violation is one involving essential services which a landlord
fails to supply contrary to the rental agreement, or if such violation is one giving
rise to a hazardous condition which materially and immediately affects health and
safety, the tenant affected by the condition may, in the alternative to the remedy
set forth above, after the city's deadline for compliance has passed, notify the landlord
in writing of the tenant's intention to:
(1)
Procure reasonable amounts of heat, hot water, running water, electricity, gas or
other essential service during the period of the landlord's noncompliance and deduct
their cost from the rent; or
(2)
Procure substitute housing during the period of the landlord's noncompliance, in which
case the tenant is excused from paying rent for the period of the landlord's noncompliance.
The tenant's actual cost of substitute housing may be deducted from the rent, provided
that the amount deducted shall not exceed the average cost for a hotel/motel room
in Urbana.
(c)
If the landlord fails to provide essential services or to correct the hazardous condition
within the time specified in the notice to correct the cited housing code violation
or any extension granted by the building official, or if any such similar uncorrected
condition or uncorrected interruption of services for any significant period recurs
and is cited by the city more than three (3) times in any twelve-month period, the
tenant may vacate the premises and terminate the rental agreement, in which case the
tenant may recover from the landlord all rent payments not applied to rent accrued
prior to the termination of the rental agreement and all damage or security deposits
not rightfully applied to damages to the rental unit.
(d)
The provisions of this section may not be used by the tenant more than three (3) times
during any twelve-month period nor may the combined total dollar amount so deducted
or excused during any such period exceed two (2) months' rent. If the tenant proceeds
under this section, the tenant may not proceed under any other sections for such breach.
(e)
The tenant may not exercise his or her rights under this section if the condition
was caused by the inability or unwillingness of a utility supplier to provide service
or by the deliberate or negligent act or omission of the tenant, a member of his or
her family, or other person on the premises with the tenant's consent.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

legal_sources.law: Residential Lead-Based Paint Hazard Reduction Act
legal_sources.text:
(27)  Target housing
The term “target housing” means any housing constructed prior to 1978, except housing for the elderly or persons with disabilities or any 0-bedroom dwelling (unless any child who is less than 6 years of age resides or is expected to reside in such housing). In the case of jurisdictions which banned the sale or use of lead-based paint prior to 1978, the Secretary, at the Secretary’s discretion, may designate an earlier date.
legal_sources.source_version: OLRC text through Public Law 119-124 (2026-10-15)
legal_sources.applicability: Definition of target housing; construction before 1978 and the enumerated exceptions must be established, not inferred from a missing clause.

legal_sources.law: Residential Lead-Based Paint Hazard Reduction Act
legal_sources.text:
(1)  Lead-based paint hazards
Not later than 2 years after October 28, 1992, the Secretary and the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency shall promulgate regulations under this section for the disclosure of lead-based paint hazards in target housing which is offered for sale or lease. The regulations shall require that, before the purchaser or lessee is obligated under any contract to purchase or lease the housing, the seller or lessor shall⁠—
(A)  provide the purchaser or lessee with a lead hazard information pamphlet, as prescribed by the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency under section 406 of the Toxic Substances Control Act [15 U.S.C. 2686];
(B)  disclose to the purchaser or lessee the presence of any known lead-based paint, or any known lead-based paint hazards, in such housing and provide to the purchaser or lessee any lead hazard evaluation report available to the seller or lessor; and
(C)  permit the purchaser a 10-day period (unless the parties mutually agree upon a different period of time) to conduct a risk assessment or inspection for the presence of lead-based paint hazards.
legal_sources.source_version: OLRC text through Public Law 119-124 (2026-10-15)
legal_sources.applicability: Target-housing disclosure framework; the ten-day inspection language is for a purchaser, not a universal tenant inspection period. Check implementing-rule exceptions separately.

result.legal_scope: Urbana, Illinois 住宅租赁：市条例、伊利诺伊州法及联邦法参考。房产须在 Urbana 市界内；本工具尚未核验市界，邮寄地址或地区选择不等于市界确认。市条例采用文件标识为 20260417 的官方导出版本，需核对后续修订及各条适用条件。
result.disclaimer: 仅供理解合同，不构成法律意见。原文匹配和法条引用核对不保证法律适用或分析结论正确。

result.summary: 这是一份极简的住宅租赁文本，仅包含两处实质内容：租客同意维修已指明的住房法典违规以换取减租，以及该约定只是格式租约中的陈述、没有磋商证据。按所给测试事实，该住宅位于 Urbana 市界内、属于普通住宅租赁且不适用第 12.5-2 条排除情形，因此 Urbana 第 12.5 章可能适用；但合同未写明房龄、楼栋单位数、押金、租金、期限、费用、进入规则、续租与通知等事项，这些均需核实。核心风险是：租客承担维修义务的安排在文本上仅为格式条款陈述，缺少 Urbana 第 12.5-18 条所要求的知情、自愿且实际磋商证据，房东须承担证明责任；这不等于该条款必然无效，需结合实际磋商过程判断。

cards.title: 格式租约中的租客维修承诺缺少磋商证据
cards.clause_text: Tenant agrees to repair identified housing-code violations in exchange for a rent reduction. This is a recital in a form lease; no bargaining evidence is supplied.
cards.explanation: 该条把修复已指明住房法典违规的义务放在租客一方，仅以减租作为对价，且合同自述这是格式租约中的陈述、没有磋商证据。按 Urbana 第 12.5-18 条，租客可明知且有意地选择承担使房屋符合住房法典的维修义务，但举证责任在房东；仅格式租约中的概括承诺不足以证明存在实际磋商。因此该条款是否可执行取决于房东能否证明租客被告知相关条款和现有违规、确实自愿选择并实际磋商，以及减租等诱因；现有文本本身不能证明这些条件已满足，也不能据此断言条款必然无效。
cards.suggestion: 签约前要求房东以书面方式列明每一项被指明的住房法典违规、减租金额与计算方式，并保留双方就该维修安排实际协商的往来记录；如无充分磋商，考虑删除该条或改为由房东负责修复。签约后保留房屋状况照片、违规通知和减租支付记录。

cards.title: 维修范围与减租对价不明确
cards.clause_text: Tenant agrees to repair identified housing-code violations in exchange for a rent reduction.
cards.explanation: 条文只说修复“已指明”的违规并换取“减租”，但合同没有列出具体违规项目、维修标准、完成期限、减租金额或减租期间。若实际履行中双方对“已指明”的范围或减租幅度理解不同，租客可能承担超出预期的维修成本，或无法证明应得的减租。该条本身不直接违法，但履行内容高度不确定。
cards.suggestion: 在签约前把违规清单、维修规格、验收方式、减租金额及支付方式写入合同附件；对每项维修保留报价、发票和完工照片，避免口头约定。

cards.title: 合同缺失押金、费用、进入、续租与通知条款
cards.clause_text: RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT. Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant.
cards.explanation: 合同正文几乎没有约定租金、期限、押金、滞纳金、其他费用、房东进入住宅的程序、续租或终止通知等事项。缺少这些内容会使双方权利义务不清，日后容易就费用、进入或续租发生争议。所给法条对押金利息、押金返还、滞纳金、费用通知、进入程序和续租通知设有具体规则，但是否适用取决于押金金额、持有时间、楼栋单位数、房龄、租约签订时间等尚未核实的事实；不能仅因合同未写就断言违反上述规定。
cards.suggestion: 签约前要求补充完整租期、租金、押金金额及返还条件、各项费用、房东进入住宅的通知程序、续租与终止通知方式；并核实房龄、楼栋单位数、押金是否达到 100 美元及是否持有超过六个月，以判断 Urbana 押金利息规则是否适用。

cards.title: 住房法典违规披露与维修责任分配需核实
cards.clause_text: Tenant agrees to repair identified housing-code violations in exchange for a rent reduction.
cards.explanation: Urbana 第 12.5-18 条要求房东在租客首次签约或续租前，书面披露建筑官员已指出且尚未纠正的住房法典违规。合同提到“已指明的违规”，但没有附披露文件，也没有说明这些违规是否已由建筑官员正式指出。若确有已指出而未纠正的违规，披露义务和维修责任分配需要进一步核实；现有文本不足以判断披露是否合规。
cards.suggestion: 向房东索取书面违规披露及建筑官员通知的副本；如房东无法提供，签约前自行向 Urbana 建筑部门核实该地址的违规记录，并保留查询结果。

(a)
If the landlord elects to terminate a month to month tenancy, or the landlord elects
to not renew the rental agreement, or to change the terms of the rental agreement
upon renewal, the landlord shall notify the tenant, in writing, not less than thirty
(30) days prior to the last day of the rental period.
(b)
If the landlord fails to give the required written notice that the rental agreement
will not be renewed, the tenant may remain in the rental unit on a month to month
basis under the same other terms and conditions as the prior term, until such time
as the required notice is given and becomes operative as set forth in subsection (a).
The tenant shall be obligated to pay rent in a timely fashion.
(c)
If the rental agreement is an oral agreement creating a month-to-month tenancy, the
tenant shall notify the landlord, in writing, not less than thirty (30) days prior
to the last day of the rental period, of the tenant's intention to vacate the premises
by the last day of the rental period.
(d)
If the tenant fails to give the required written notice to terminate the oral rental
agreement, the tenant shall be liable to the landlord for lost rent during the time
that the rental unit remains vacant, until the end of the next rental period, except
that the tenant shall not be liable for payment of said lost rent if the landlord
failed to provide the tenant with notice of the tenant's obligations as described
in section 12.5-12 of this Code. The landlord shall have a duty to mitigate damages.
(e)
The written notice required by this section may be delivered by personal service,
first class mail, or any other means reasonably intended to provide actual notice.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

legal_sources.text:
(a)
The tenant shall not unreasonably withhold consent to the landlord to enter the rental
unit in order to inspect the premises, make necessary or agreed repairs, supply necessary
or agreed services, make alterations or improvements if such alterations or improvements
do not interfere with the tenant's use of the premises, or to show the rental unit
to prospective or actual purchasers, mortgagees or tenants.
(b)
The landlord shall not abuse the right of access to the rental unit or use it to harass
the tenant. Except in cases of emergency or by mutual consent, the landlord or landlord's
agents shall not enter the rental unit without first providing the tenant with at
least twenty-four (24) hours advance notice of the entry and may enter only at reasonable
times. Reasonable times shall be considered 10:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on weekdays and
11:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on weekends, or such other times agreed upon by the tenant
and the landlord.
(c)
From the time that either the landlord or the tenant notifies the other party that
the rental agreement will not be renewed, the landlord shall have the right to access,
without twenty-four (24) hours advance notice, for the purpose of showing the rental
unit to prospective tenants, provided that:
(1)
The rental unit has not already been leased for the twelve-month period subsequent
to the expiration of the rental agreement;
(2)
The landlord enters only during two (2) specific one-hour periods on weekdays and
three (3) specific one-hour periods on weekends, selected by the tenant from among
choices offered by the landlord, during which the landlord will have daily access;
and
(3)
The landlord shall notify the tenant when the rental unit has been leased for the
twelve-month period subsequent to the expiration of the rental agreement.
(d)
If the tenant requests repairs and the landlord enters the rental unit to perform
said repairs within fourteen (14) days of the tenant's initial request, the landlord
shall not be obligated to provide the tenant with advance notice of entry. If the
landlord fails to perform said repairs within fourteen (14) days of the tenant's initial
request, the landlord shall be required to provide the tenant with at least twenty-four
(24) hours' advance notice of entry. The notice shall only be effective for a seven-day
period.
(e)
The landlord may enter the rental unit at any time, without advance notice, in case
of emergency. For purposes of this provision, the term "emergency" shall refer to
a situation wherein access to the rental unit is necessary in order to prevent damage
or destruction to the rental unit, other rental units, or the building, or to the
fixtures, equipment, appliances, furniture or other personal property contained therein,
or in order to protect any person from injury. Nonpayment or delinquent payment of
rent shall not constitute an emergency.
(f)
The landlord or landlord's agents shall enter the rental unit only after knocking
on the door and providing the tenant a reasonable opportunity to answer, shall leave
the premises in as good condition as when entered, shall clean and remove dirt and
debris that result from the performance of maintenance and repairs, shall leave a
note indicating the names of the persons who entered the rental unit and shall lock
the rental unit when leaving.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

legal_sources.text:
(a)
The landlord shall maintain the premises in compliance with all applicable housing
codes of the city and shall promptly make any and all necessary repairs to fulfill
that obligation, provided, however, that the tenant may knowingly and intentionally
elect and agree to repair the premises to bring them into conformity with the applicable
housing codes of the city. The burden shall be on the landlord to establish a knowing
and intentional election on the part of the tenant to repair the premises in compliance
with the applicable housing code. A mere recital in a form lease that tenant has covenanted
to repair will not be sufficient, it being the intention of this article that any
agreement with the tenant to repair be bargained for in fact. A separate hand-written
paragraph in the lease showing:
(1)
That the tenant has been informed of this article and the existing code violations;
(2)
That he/she has affirmatively elected and bargained to repair the violations listed
and other items listed; and
(3)
The inducement for such arrangements, will be prima facie evidence that such provision
was entered into in good faith and was bargained for in fact.
(b)
Nothing in this article shall be interpreted so as to restrict the authority of city
inspectors to cite a landlord for violation of building code provisions.
(c)
Before a tenant initially enters into or renews a rental agreement for a rental unit,
the landlord or any person authorized to enter into a rental agreement on the landlord's
behalf shall disclose to the tenant in writing any housing code violations which have
been cited by the building official and which remain uncorrected for that rental unit
and the common area of the premises.
(d)
This article shall not be interpreted as decreasing or diminishing the implied warranty
of habitability as adopted by the Illinois Supreme Court.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

result.disclaimer: 仅供理解合同，不构成法律意见。原文匹配和法条引用核对不保证法律适用或分析结论正确。

result.summary: 本合同为普通住宅租约，文本仅含标题、租赁关系声明及一段关于“打字附件列明法规违规与减租”的测试性事实说明，未提供具体条款原文。因此无法逐条审查租金、押金、进入、维修、驱逐、续租等实际安排。需注意：所给事实称承租人知情并实际协商了维修与减租，但附件未手写；在 Urbana 第12.5-18条下，手写段落只是“初步证据”而非唯一形式，房东仍须证明该维修安排是知情、自愿且实际协商的。合同是否属于 Urbana 第12.5章适用范围、房龄、楼栋单元数、押金金额及是否使用收费支付门户等均需核实。

cards.title: 维修与减租安排缺少手写段落，需核实是否确为实际协商
cards.clause_text: A typed attachment identifies code violations and a rent reduction. Stipulated facts: Tenant knew of the violations and the ordinance, intentionally elected to repair, and actually negotiated the listed repairs and reduction. Negotiation records exist, but no paragraph is handwritten.
cards.explanation: Urbana 第12.5-18条允许承租人在知情且实际协商的情况下承担修复义务，但房东须证明该选择是知情、自愿且实际协商的；仅凭格式租约中的声明不足以证明。该条把“单独手写段落”列为初步证据，但并未规定它是唯一可接受的证明形式。所给事实称存在协商记录且承租人知情，但附件为打字文本、无手写段落，因此该维修/减租安排能否被认定为有效“实际协商”仍需结合记录核实，不能仅凭缺少手写段落就断言无效。
cards.suggestion: 保留能证明承租人知情、自愿选择维修并实际协商减租的往来记录、附件签署页和减租计算依据；签约前请房东书面确认该附件属于双方协商条款，并核对所列违规项目与减租金额是否一致。

cards.title: 附件所列法规违规与减租安排的具体内容未提供，无法评估
cards.clause_text: A typed attachment identifies code violations and a rent reduction.
cards.explanation: 合同正文未列出具体违规项目、修复期限、减租金额及减租起算方式。若附件内容不明确，可能影响承租人主张维修、减租或后续救济时的举证。该条本身不当然违法，但执行效果取决于附件是否具体、可核对。
cards.suggestion: 签约前取得完整附件，逐项核对违规编号、修复责任方、完成期限、减租金额及计算方式；如附件缺失或含糊，要求房东补充书面说明后再签。

cards.title: 押金利息与退还规则未在合同中体现，需核实适用条件
cards.clause_text: RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT. Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant.
cards.explanation: 合同未提供押金金额、保管及退还条款。Urbana 第12.5-19条对100美元以上、持有超过六个月的押金设有本地利息规则；第12.5-20条对损坏扣款的事前明细、收据和退还期限有要求。是否适用取决于押金金额、持有时间及是否属于第12.5章适用范围，目前均需核实，不能仅因合同未写就认定违法。
cards.suggestion: 签约前书面确认押金金额、退还期限和扣款程序；退租时保留入住与退租照片、交接记录，并书面提供押金退还地址。

cards.title: 进入住宅、驱逐及续租通知条款缺失，需补充核实
cards.clause_text: RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT. Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant.
cards.explanation: 合同文本未包含房东进入住宅、驱逐程序或续租通知的具体条款。Urbana 第12.5-15条对提前24小时通知、合理时间及紧急进入设有规则；第12.5-11条对不续租或变更条款设有30天书面通知要求；第12.5-25条禁止未经法院授权的自助驱逐。合同未写并不等于房东可不受这些规则约束，但实际适用仍取决于该租约是否属于第12.5章范围及具体事实。
cards.suggestion: 要求房东在租约中写明进入通知方式、续租通知期限和驱逐须经法院程序；保留所有进入通知与续租沟通记录。

cards.title: 支付方式与费用条款未提供，需核实是否强制电子支付或收取额外费用
cards.clause_text: RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT. Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant.
cards.explanation: 合同未说明租金支付方式及是否通过第三方门户收取交易费。伊利诺伊州法对2024年1月1日后签订的租约禁止强制以电子资金转账方式支付租金；对2025年1月1日后签订且门户收取交易费的租约，房东须允许无额外费用的纸质支票或现金支付。本租约签订于2026年，但合同未提供支付条款，是否适用及是否存在违规需核实。
cards.suggestion: 签约前确认是否必须使用电子支付、是否产生交易费，并要求书面列明不收费的替代支付方式；保留每次付款凭证。

legal_sources.text:
(a)
If the landlord elects to terminate a month to month tenancy, or the landlord elects
to not renew the rental agreement, or to change the terms of the rental agreement
upon renewal, the landlord shall notify the tenant, in writing, not less than thirty
(30) days prior to the last day of the rental period.
(b)
If the landlord fails to give the required written notice that the rental agreement
will not be renewed, the tenant may remain in the rental unit on a month to month
basis under the same other terms and conditions as the prior term, until such time
as the required notice is given and becomes operative as set forth in subsection (a).
The tenant shall be obligated to pay rent in a timely fashion.
(c)
If the rental agreement is an oral agreement creating a month-to-month tenancy, the
tenant shall notify the landlord, in writing, not less than thirty (30) days prior
to the last day of the rental period, of the tenant's intention to vacate the premises
by the last day of the rental period.
(d)
If the tenant fails to give the required written notice to terminate the oral rental
agreement, the tenant shall be liable to the landlord for lost rent during the time
that the rental unit remains vacant, until the end of the next rental period, except
that the tenant shall not be liable for payment of said lost rent if the landlord
failed to provide the tenant with notice of the tenant's obligations as described
in section 12.5-12 of this Code. The landlord shall have a duty to mitigate damages.
(e)
The written notice required by this section may be delivered by personal service,
first class mail, or any other means reasonably intended to provide actual notice.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

legal_sources.text:
(a)
The tenant shall not unreasonably withhold consent to the landlord to enter the rental
unit in order to inspect the premises, make necessary or agreed repairs, supply necessary
or agreed services, make alterations or improvements if such alterations or improvements
do not interfere with the tenant's use of the premises, or to show the rental unit
to prospective or actual purchasers, mortgagees or tenants.
(b)
The landlord shall not abuse the right of access to the rental unit or use it to harass
the tenant. Except in cases of emergency or by mutual consent, the landlord or landlord's
agents shall not enter the rental unit without first providing the tenant with at
least twenty-four (24) hours advance notice of the entry and may enter only at reasonable
times. Reasonable times shall be considered 10:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on weekdays and
11:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on weekends, or such other times agreed upon by the tenant
and the landlord.
(c)
From the time that either the landlord or the tenant notifies the other party that
the rental agreement will not be renewed, the landlord shall have the right to access,
without twenty-four (24) hours advance notice, for the purpose of showing the rental
unit to prospective tenants, provided that:
(1)
The rental unit has not already been leased for the twelve-month period subsequent
to the expiration of the rental agreement;
(2)
The landlord enters only during two (2) specific one-hour periods on weekdays and
three (3) specific one-hour periods on weekends, selected by the tenant from among
choices offered by the landlord, during which the landlord will have daily access;
and
(3)
The landlord shall notify the tenant when the rental unit has been leased for the
twelve-month period subsequent to the expiration of the rental agreement.
(d)
If the tenant requests repairs and the landlord enters the rental unit to perform
said repairs within fourteen (14) days of the tenant's initial request, the landlord
shall not be obligated to provide the tenant with advance notice of entry. If the
landlord fails to perform said repairs within fourteen (14) days of the tenant's initial
request, the landlord shall be required to provide the tenant with at least twenty-four
(24) hours' advance notice of entry. The notice shall only be effective for a seven-day
period.
(e)
The landlord may enter the rental unit at any time, without advance notice, in case
of emergency. For purposes of this provision, the term "emergency" shall refer to
a situation wherein access to the rental unit is necessary in order to prevent damage
or destruction to the rental unit, other rental units, or the building, or to the
fixtures, equipment, appliances, furniture or other personal property contained therein,
or in order to protect any person from injury. Nonpayment or delinquent payment of
rent shall not constitute an emergency.
(f)
The landlord or landlord's agents shall enter the rental unit only after knocking
on the door and providing the tenant a reasonable opportunity to answer, shall leave
the premises in as good condition as when entered, shall clean and remove dirt and
debris that result from the performance of maintenance and repairs, shall leave a
note indicating the names of the persons who entered the rental unit and shall lock
the rental unit when leaving.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

legal_sources.text:
(a)
The landlord shall maintain the premises in compliance with all applicable housing
codes of the city and shall promptly make any and all necessary repairs to fulfill
that obligation, provided, however, that the tenant may knowingly and intentionally
elect and agree to repair the premises to bring them into conformity with the applicable
housing codes of the city. The burden shall be on the landlord to establish a knowing
and intentional election on the part of the tenant to repair the premises in compliance
with the applicable housing code. A mere recital in a form lease that tenant has covenanted
to repair will not be sufficient, it being the intention of this article that any
agreement with the tenant to repair be bargained for in fact. A separate hand-written
paragraph in the lease showing:
(1)
That the tenant has been informed of this article and the existing code violations;
(2)
That he/she has affirmatively elected and bargained to repair the violations listed
and other items listed; and
(3)
The inducement for such arrangements, will be prima facie evidence that such provision
was entered into in good faith and was bargained for in fact.
(b)
Nothing in this article shall be interpreted so as to restrict the authority of city
inspectors to cite a landlord for violation of building code provisions.
(c)
Before a tenant initially enters into or renews a rental agreement for a rental unit,
the landlord or any person authorized to enter into a rental agreement on the landlord's
behalf shall disclose to the tenant in writing any housing code violations which have
been cited by the building official and which remain uncorrected for that rental unit
and the common area of the premises.
(d)
This article shall not be interpreted as decreasing or diminishing the implied warranty
of habitability as adopted by the Illinois Supreme Court.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

A tenant repair election must be knowing, intentional and actually bargained for, with the burden on the landlord; a form-lease recital alone is insufficient. The described separate handwritten paragraph is prima facie evidence, not stated as the sole permissible form of proof. Distinguish payment allocation from an agreement to perform code-compliance repairs, and verify the particular repair and bargaining facts.

legal_sources.text:
(a)
A landlord who receives a security deposit of one hundred dollars ($100.00) or more
from a tenant to secure the payment of rent or to compensate for damage to property
shall pay interest to the tenant, computed from the date the deposit is paid, at a
rate equal to the interest paid by the largest commercial bank, as measured by total
assets, having its main banking premises in Champaign County, Illinois, on minimum
deposit passbook savings accounts as of the thirtieth of June immediately preceding
the inception of the rental agreement on any such deposit held by the landlord for
more than six (6) months.
(b)
The landlord shall, within thirty (30) days after the end of each twelve-month rental
period, pay to the tenant any interest, by cash or credit to be applied to rent due,
except when the tenant is in default under the terms of the lease. For the purposes
of this provision, default shall mean nonpayment of rent or a successful claim by
the landlord for possession of the premises for good cause other than nonpayment of
rent. A landlord who willfully fails or refuses to pay the interest required by this
article shall, upon a finding by a circuit court that he/she has willfully failed
or refused to pay, be liable for an amount equal to the amount of the security deposit,
together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

legal_sources.text:
(a)
A lessor of residential real property who has received a security deposit from a lessee
to secure the payment of rent or to compensate for damage to the leased property may
not withhold any part of that deposit as compensation for property damage unless he
or she has, within thirty (30) days of the date that the lessee vacated the premises,
furnished to the lessee, delivered in person or by mail directed to his or her last
known address, an itemized statement of the damage allegedly caused to the premises
and the estimated or actual cost for repairing or replacing each item on that statement,
attaching the paid receipts, or copies thereof, for the repair or replacement. If
the lessor utilizes his or her own labor to repair any damage caused by the lessee,
the lessor may include the reasonable cost of his or her labor to repair such damage.
If estimated cost is given, the lessor shall furnish the lessee with paid receipts,
or copies thereof, within thirty (30) days from the date the statement showing estimated
cost was furnished to the lessee, as required by this section. If no such statement
and receipts, or copies thereof, are furnished to the lessee as required by this section,
the lessor shall return the security deposit in full within forty-five (45) days of
the date that the lessee vacated the premises.
(b)
Upon a finding by a circuit court that the landlord has refused to supply the itemized
statement required herein, or has supplied such statement in bad faith, and has failed
or refused to return the amount of the security deposit due within the time limits
provided, the landlord shall be liable for an amount equal to twice the amount of
the security deposit due, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
(c)
Reserved.
(d)
The decorating of the rental unit after the tenant vacates, including painting and
carpet cleaning, unless walls or carpets are damaged beyond normal wear, shall not
be considered as damage and the costs thereof shall not be charged to the security
deposit.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94; Ord. No. 2000-07-066, 7-17-00)

(a)
It is unlawful for any landlord or any person acting at the direction of the landlord
to knowingly oust or dispossess or attempt to oust or dispossess any tenant from a

legal_sources.text: Sec. 3.5. Additional means to pay rent when electronic payment methods charge additional fees. If a landlord uses a third-party payment portal to collect rental payments from tenants and if a transaction fee or other charge is imposed through the portal on rental payments made by e-check or other means, then the landlord shall allow the tenant to make rental payments by delivering a paper check or cash to the landlord or the landlord's business office or by means that do not require the tenant to pay the transaction fee or other charge. This Section applies to leases or agreements executed after the effective date of this amendatory Act of the 103rd General Assembly.
legal_sources.applicability: Applies to agreements executed after the 2025 effective date, when a third-party portal imposes a transaction fee.

legal_sources.text:
Sec. 4. Payment by electronic funds transfer.
(a) As used in this Section, "electronic funds transfer" means a transfer of funds, other than a transaction originated by check, draft, or similar paper instrument, that is initiated through an electronic terminal, telephone, computer, or magnetic tape for the purpose of ordering, instructing, or authorizing a financial institution to debit or credit a consumer's account, including, but not limited to, through the use of an automated clearing house system.
(b) A landlord shall not require a tenant or prospective tenant to remit any amount due to the landlord under a residential lease, renewal, or extension agreement by means of an electronic funds transfer, including, but not limited to, an electronic funds transfer system that automatically transfers funds on a regular, periodic, and recurring basis.
(c) Beginning 90 days after the effective date of this amendatory Act of the 103rd General Assembly, a landlord who violates this Section is guilty of an unlawful practice under the Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Business Practices Act.
(d) This Section applies to leases or agreements executed after the effective date of this amendatory Act of the 103rd General Assembly.
legal_sources.applicability: Applies to agreements executed after the 2024 effective date; civil-enforcement timing is separately specified in subsection (c).

result.summary: 该合同文本极短，仅包含一条关于租期结束后处置租客遗留财物的条款，其余租赁核心事项（租金、押金、维修、进入、续租、驱逐程序等）均未出现，需另行核实完整租约。就现有文字看，主要风险是房东在租期终止后对价值极低的遗留物可立即丢弃，可能使租客来不及取回物品；该安排与 Urbana 法典 12.5-22(c) 中“价值极低、仓储成本超过变卖所得即可立即处置”的例外在文本上相符，但“$5 售价、$100 仓储成本”属于合同自述事实，实际是否成立需核实。另需注意：合同自述位于 Urbana 市界内、属普通住宅租赁且不适用第 12.5-2 条排除情形，这是测试性约定，并非独立核实的市界查询结果；若实际不在市界内或属于排除情形，Urbana 第 12.5 章不适用。

cards.title: 租期终止后低值遗留物可被立即丢弃
cards.clause_text: After tenancy termination, Landlord may immediately discard property reasonably believed to have a $5 sale value when storage would cost $100.
cards.explanation: 该条允许房东在租期终止后，对“合理认为变卖价值仅 $5、而仓储成本为 $100”的财物不经 30 天通知即直接丢弃。Urbana 法典 12.5-22(c) 确实允许在房东合理认为财物无价值或价值低到仓储成本超过变卖所得时立即处置，因此该文字本身与法条例外方向一致；但“$5 价值、$100 仓储成本”是合同单方设定的事实，实际处置时是否真的满足该例外、房东的判断是否合理，均需个案核实。若实际不满足例外，租客可能面临财物被过早丢弃且难以追回的风险。
cards.suggestion: 签约前要求房东书面说明该条仅适用于经合理判断确属低值或易腐的财物，并保留对非低值物品的 30 天通知与领取程序；入住及退租时拍照清点个人财物，退租前书面确认搬离时间与遗留物处理方式，必要时保留财物价值凭证。

cards.title: 合同缺少押金、维修、进入、续租等核心条款
cards.clause_text: RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT. Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant.
cards.explanation: 现有文本只有一句概括性租赁声明和一条遗留物处置条款，未写明租金、押金金额与退还、维修责任、房东进入住宅的通知程序、续租或终止通知、费用与滞纳金等事项。缺少这些内容本身不证明违法，但会使双方权利义务高度不确定，日后争议时难以依据合同文字判断。Urbana 第 12.5 章对其中多项事项有规定，但适用前提是该出租单元位于 Urbana 市界内且不属于第 12.5-2 条排除情形；合同自述的测试性事实不能替代实际核实。
cards.suggestion: 签署前索取完整租约及附件，逐项核对租金、押金、维修、进入通知、续租与终止、费用条款；确认房屋是否确在 Urbana 市界内、是否属于第 12.5-2 条排除情形，并保留完整签署版本。

legal_sources.text:
This chapter applies to, regulates and determines certain rights, obligations and
remedies under a rental agreement for a rental unit located within the city. Unless
created to avoid the application of this chapter, however, the following arrangements
are not governed by this chapter:
(1)
Residence at an institution, public or private, if incidental to detention or the
provision of medical, geriatric, counseling, religious or similar service;
(2)
Occupancy under a contract of sale of a rental unit or the property of which it is
a part, if the occupant is the purchaser or a person who succeeds to his/her interest;

Occupancy by a member of a fraternal or social organization in the portion of a structure

Transient occupancy in a hotel, motel tourist home or tourist court;

Occupancy by an employee of a landlord whose right to occupancy is conditional upon
employment in and about the premises.

legal_sources.text:
(a)
The tenant shall not unreasonably withhold consent to the landlord to enter the rental
unit in order to inspect the premises, make necessary or agreed repairs, supply necessary
or agreed services, make alterations or improvements if such alterations or improvements
do not interfere with the tenant's use of the premises, or to show the rental unit
to prospective or actual purchasers, mortgagees or tenants.
(b)
The landlord shall not abuse the right of access to the rental unit or use it to harass
the tenant. Except in cases of emergency or by mutual consent, the landlord or landlord's
agents shall not enter the rental unit without first providing the tenant with at
least twenty-four (24) hours advance notice of the entry and may enter only at reasonable
times. Reasonable times shall be considered 10:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on weekdays and
11:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on weekends, or such other times agreed upon by the tenant
and the landlord.
(c)
From the time that either the landlord or the tenant notifies the other party that
the rental agreement will not be renewed, the landlord shall have the right to access,
without twenty-four (24) hours advance notice, for the purpose of showing the rental
unit to prospective tenants, provided that:
(1)
The rental unit has not already been leased for the twelve-month period subsequent
to the expiration of the rental agreement;
(2)
The landlord enters only during two (2) specific one-hour periods on weekdays and
three (3) specific one-hour periods on weekends, selected by the tenant from among
choices offered by the landlord, during which the landlord will have daily access;
and
(3)
The landlord shall notify the tenant when the rental unit has been leased for the
twelve-month period subsequent to the expiration of the rental agreement.
(d)
If the tenant requests repairs and the landlord enters the rental unit to perform
said repairs within fourteen (14) days of the tenant's initial request, the landlord
shall not be obligated to provide the tenant with advance notice of entry. If the
landlord fails to perform said repairs within fourteen (14) days of the tenant's initial
request, the landlord shall be required to provide the tenant with at least twenty-four
(24) hours' advance notice of entry. The notice shall only be effective for a seven-day
period.
(e)
The landlord may enter the rental unit at any time, without advance notice, in case
of emergency. For purposes of this provision, the term "emergency" shall refer to
a situation wherein access to the rental unit is necessary in order to prevent damage
or destruction to the rental unit, other rental units, or the building, or to the
fixtures, equipment, appliances, furniture or other personal property contained therein,
or in order to protect any person from injury. Nonpayment or delinquent payment of
rent shall not constitute an emergency.
(f)
The landlord or landlord's agents shall enter the rental unit only after knocking
on the door and providing the tenant a reasonable opportunity to answer, shall leave
the premises in as good condition as when entered, shall clean and remove dirt and
debris that result from the performance of maintenance and repairs, shall leave a
note indicating the names of the persons who entered the rental unit and shall lock
the rental unit when leaving.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

legal_sources.text:
(a)
A lessor of residential real property who has received a security deposit from a lessee
to secure the payment of rent or to compensate for damage to the leased property may
not withhold any part of that deposit as compensation for property damage unless he
or she has, within thirty (30) days of the date that the lessee vacated the premises,
furnished to the lessee, delivered in person or by mail directed to his or her last
known address, an itemized statement of the damage allegedly caused to the premises
and the estimated or actual cost for repairing or replacing each item on that statement,
attaching the paid receipts, or copies thereof, for the repair or replacement. If
the lessor utilizes his or her own labor to repair any damage caused by the lessee,
the lessor may include the reasonable cost of his or her labor to repair such damage.
If estimated cost is given, the lessor shall furnish the lessee with paid receipts,
or copies thereof, within thirty (30) days from the date the statement showing estimated
cost was furnished to the lessee, as required by this section. If no such statement
and receipts, or copies thereof, are furnished to the lessee as required by this section,
the lessor shall return the security deposit in full within forty-five (45) days of
the date that the lessee vacated the premises.
(b)
Upon a finding by a circuit court that the landlord has refused to supply the itemized
statement required herein, or has supplied such statement in bad faith, and has failed
or refused to return the amount of the security deposit due within the time limits
provided, the landlord shall be liable for an amount equal to twice the amount of
the security deposit due, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
(c)
Reserved.
(d)
The decorating of the rental unit after the tenant vacates, including painting and
carpet cleaning, unless walls or carpets are damaged beyond normal wear, shall not
be considered as damage and the costs thereof shall not be charged to the security
deposit.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94; Ord. No. 2000-07-066, 7-17-00)

legal_sources.text:
(a)
The tenant shall be deemed to have abandoned the rental unit by being absent with
visible intent not to return and with rent unpaid.
(b)
If the tenant abandons the rental unit, the landlord may take possession of the rental
unit.
(c)
If the tenant abandons the rental unit or fails to remove his or her personal property
from the premises after termination of a rental agreement, the landlord shall leave
the abandoned property in the rental unit or remove and store all abandoned property
from the rental unit. The landlord may charge the tenant for the actual costs of storage.
The landlord may dispose of the property thirty (30) days after mailing written notice
to tenant's last known address, if the tenant does not claim the property within that
time. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the landlord reasonably believes such abandoned
property to be valueless or of such little value that the cost of storage would exceed
the amount that would be realized from sale, or if such property is subject to spoilage,
the landlord may immediately dispose of such property.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)
legal_sources.source_version: User-supplied Municode export labeled 20260417; workbook export metadata 2026-10-28; subsequent amendments must be checked
legal_sources.applicability: Subject to Secs. 12.5-2 and 12.5-7. Abandonment of a unit under (a) requires absence with visible intent not to return and unpaid rent; do not infer it from absence alone. Under (c), preserve the mailed-notice, 30-day and non-claim conditions. Immediate disposal also covers property reasonably believed to have such little value that storage would exceed sale proceeds, as well as valueless or perishable property.

cards.title: 终止后立即丢弃未取走财物，缺少通知与等待期
cards.clause_text: After tenancy termination, Landlord may immediately discard any uncollected property.
cards.explanation: 该条允许房东在租期终止后立即丢弃所有未取走财物，未区分价值、是否易腐，也未要求向租客最后已知地址邮寄通知或等待 30 天。按诊断设定，该非易腐物品售价约 1000 美元、存储成本约 50 美元，不存在可合理认为无价值或低价值的情形，且未邮寄通知；因此该条文字与 Urbana 第 12.5-22(c) 条规定的通知、30 天等待及低价值/易腐例外不一致。该条是否可执行及租客可获何种救济，仍需结合具体事实和程序判断，不能仅凭本条断言必然违法或无效。
cards.suggestion: 签约前要求删除“立即丢弃”表述，改为：终止后房东应保留或存储财物，向租客最后已知地址邮寄书面通知，30 天内未认领方可处置；仅对合理认为无价值、低价值或易腐物品可立即处置。入住后保留财物价值凭证、存储费用证据及通知记录。

cards.title: 合同缺少租金、租期与押金等核心条款，权利义务不明
cards.clause_text: RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT. Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant. Premises: 1 Main Street, Urbana, IL.
cards.explanation: 文本未写明租金金额、支付方式与时间、租期、押金数额及退还条件、维修责任、进入规则、续租与终止方式。这些空白本身不证明任何条款违法，但会使双方在履约中各自解释，日后就欠租、扣款、退租或续租发生争议时缺乏书面依据。
cards.suggestion: 签署前要求提供完整书面租约，逐项确认租金、到期日、押金、费用、维修、进入通知、续租与终止条款，并保留完整签署版本及所有附件。

cards.title: 未确认房屋是否位于 Urbana 市界内，地方规则适用性待核实
cards.clause_text: Premises: 1 Main Street, Urbana, IL. User selected Urbana. No municipal-boundary evidence is supplied.
cards.explanation: Urbana 第12.5章适用于位于 Urbana 市界内的租赁单元，并受该章适用范围和例外约束。合同地址写作 Urbana 以及用户选择 Urbana，都不等于已核实房屋位于市界内；若实际不在市界内，该章的地方性保护与程序规则未必适用。这不代表合同条款当然无效，只是适用规则需先确认。
cards.suggestion: 通过 Urbana 市官方地界或分区查询工具核实地址所属市界，并保留查询结果；同时确认租约签订或续签日期，以判断第12.5章是否适用。

cards.title: 未提供房龄，铅漆披露义务无法核对
cards.clause_text: Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant.
cards.explanation: 联邦铅漆披露规则针对1978年前建造的目标住房，并要求在承租方受合同约束前提供宣传册、披露已知铅漆或铅漆危害并提供可得的评估报告。合同未写建造年份，也未附披露文件，因此无法判断是否属于目标住房、披露是否已完成；缺少条款本身不等于违法。
cards.suggestion: 向房东书面询问房屋建造年份，索取铅漆披露文件与 EPA 宣传册；如属1978年前住房且未获披露，先保留证据并咨询当地法律援助，不宜仅凭此拒付租金。

cards.title: 押金金额与退还条件未约定，扣款争议风险
cards.clause_text: RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT. Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant.
cards.explanation: 合同未写押金数额、保管方式、利息安排和退还时间。若确属 Urbana 市界内的租赁且押金达到100美元并持有超过六个月，Urbana 规则要求支付利息；州法对押金损坏扣款设有分项清单、收据和退还期限要求。上述规则均有适用条件，且目前押金事实未知，不能据此断言房东已违规。
cards.suggestion: 在租约中写明押金金额、退还期限与扣款须附分项清单和收据；入住和退租时拍照留证，退租时提供书面邮寄地址以便接收结算文件。

cards.title: 维修责任与维修抵扣程序未约定
cards.clause_text: Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant.
cards.explanation: 合同未说明房东的维修义务、租户报修方式，也未说明租户可否自行维修并抵扣租金。Urbana 规则和州维修抵扣法均设有通知、催告期、费用上限、承包商资质与保险等条件，不能未经程序直接停付或抵扣租金；合同缺失这些内容会增加操作失误风险。
cards.suggestion: 要求补充书面维修条款，明确报修渠道和时限；出现需维修情形时先书面报修并保留记录，若要行使维修抵扣权，先核对通知方式、金额上限和承包商资质等法定条件。

cards.title: 房东进入住宅的规则未约定
cards.clause_text: Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant.
cards.explanation: 合同未写房东进入住宅的通知方式、时间范围和紧急进入情形。若适用 Urbana 第12.5章，一般进入须提前至少24小时通知并限于合理时间，紧急情况等例外不受该通知限制；条款缺失使租户难以判断某次进入是否合规，但不代表房东必然违法。
cards.suggestion: 要求书面补充进入条款，写明提前通知方式、可进入时段和紧急情形定义；对每次进入记录时间、人员和事由，如认为进入不当，保留证据并咨询律师，不要自行换锁。

cards.title: 续租与终止通知机制未约定
cards.clause_text: RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT. Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant.
cards.explanation: 合同未写租期类型、到期是否自动续期、双方不续租的通知期限。Urbana 规则禁止约定因租户未通知不续租而自动续期，并对房东不续租或变更续租条件设有30日书面通知要求；这些规则以适用第12.5章为前提，目前租期与签订日期均未知。
cards.suggestion: 在租约中明确租期起止、是否自动续期以及双方不续租的书面通知期限和送达方式；保留所有续租或终止通知的副本和邮寄凭证。

cards.title: 费用与滞纳金条款缺失，收费依据不明
cards.clause_text: RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT. Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant.
cards.explanation: 合同未列明滞纳金、钥匙或换锁费、转租费、提前退租费等任何费用。若适用 Urbana 第12.5章，滞纳金须在租约中写明，且超过月租5%须有更高实际成本证明；其他费用不得超过实际成本，非租金费用还须在30日内书面通知。缺失条款使日后新增收费缺乏依据，但不能据此认定任何具体收费已违规。
cards.suggestion: 要求把所有可能收取的费用及金额写入租约；对签约后新增的任何收费要求书面说明依据和金额，并保留付款与通知记录。

cards.title: 转租与提前退租安排未约定
cards.clause_text: Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant.
cards.explanation: 合同未说明是否允许转租、需否房东同意、提前退租如何处理。Urbana 规则禁止绝对禁止转租，但允许事先同意或审核条件；州法要求房东对违约租户的损失采取合理减损措施。上述规则的具体适用取决于租约内容和事实，目前无法判断。
cards.suggestion: 在租约中写明转租申请流程和提前退租的费用计算方式；如需提前搬离，书面通知房东并保留其重新招租、减损的相关记录。

legal_sources.text:
This chapter applies to, regulates and determines certain rights, obligations and
remedies under a rental agreement for a rental unit located within the city. Unless
created to avoid the application of this chapter, however, the following arrangements
are not governed by this chapter:
(1)
Residence at an institution, public or private, if incidental to detention or the
provision of medical, geriatric, counseling, religious or similar service;
(2)
Occupancy under a contract of sale of a rental unit or the property of which it is
a part, if the occupant is the purchaser or a person who succeeds to his/her interest;
(3)
Occupancy by a member of a fraternal or social organization in the portion of a structure
operated for the benefit of the organization;
(4)
Transient occupancy in a hotel, motel tourist home or tourist court;
(5)
Occupancy by an employee of a landlord whose right to occupancy is conditional upon
employment in and about the premises.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

legal_sources.text:
(a)
Except as otherwise provided by this article, no rental agreement between the landlord
and the tenant shall contain any provision:
(1)
Waiving the rights or remedies provided under this article;
(2)
Waiving any statutory rights or remedies provided under state or federal law;
(3)
Providing that either the landlord or the tenant confess judgment on a claim arising
out of the rental agreement;
(4)
Providing that either the landlord or the tenant may recover attorney's fees incurred
to enforce the rental agreement unless the rental agreement stipulates that both the
landlord and the tenant be entitled to recovery of attorney's fees under identical
terms and conditions;
(5)
Limiting the liability of the landlord or the tenant arising under law;
(6)
Prohibiting the tenant from subletting the rental unit;
(7)
Requiring a monthly late fee in excess of five (5) percent of the monthly rental payment
per month; fees in excess of this amount may be charged if the landlord demonstrates
actual costs which are greater;
(8)
Providing for tenant's payment of lock-out charges, sublet fees, late checkout charges
or any other fees or penalties that exceed the landlord's actual costs for services;
or
(9)
Automatically renewing the rental agreement by reason of the tenant's failure to provide
notice of intent not to renew.
(b)
A provision prohibited by subsection (a) included in a rental agreement is unenforceable.
If the landlord deliberately attempts to enforce any provision in a rental agreement
which is prohibited, the tenant may recover an amount totaling not more than two (2)
months' rent and such damages, costs and reasonable attorney's fees as a court shall
determine and award. The landlord shall be considered to have deliberately attempted
to enforce a prohibited lease provision if the landlord knew or reasonably should
have known that the provision was prohibited and the landlord:
(1)
Refuses to approve a sublease as required by law or requires, as a condition of granting
approval of a sublease, payment of a prohibited sublease charge, acceleration of rent
or payment of a higher rental rate than stipulated in the lease agreement;
(2)
Refuses to provide a service because of the tenant's nonpayment of a prohibited fee
or charge;
(3)
Serves the tenant with written demand stating the intention to terminate the rental
agreement for nonpayment of prohibited fees or charges;
(4)
Files suit against the tenant to enforce the prohibited provision.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

legal_sources.text:
(a)
The tenant shall not unreasonably withhold consent to the landlord to enter the rental
unit in order to inspect the premises, make necessary or agreed repairs, supply necessary
or agreed services, make alterations or improvements if such alterations or improvements
do not interfere with the tenant's use of the premises, or to show the rental unit
to prospective or actual purchasers, mortgagees or tenants.
(b)
The landlord shall not abuse the right of access to the rental unit or use it to harass
the tenant. Except in cases of emergency or by mutual consent, the landlord or landlord's
agents shall not enter the rental unit without first providing the tenant with at
least twenty-four (24) hours advance notice of the entry and may enter only at reasonable
times. Reasonable times shall be considered 10:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on weekdays and
11:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on weekends, or such other times agreed upon by the tenant
and the landlord.
(c)
From the time that either the landlord or the tenant notifies the other party that
the rental agreement will not be renewed, the landlord shall have the right to access,
without twenty-four (24) hours advance notice, for the purpose of showing the rental
unit to prospective tenants, provided that:
(1)
The rental unit has not already been leased for the twelve-month period subsequent
to the expiration of the rental agreement;
(2)
The landlord enters only during two (2) specific one-hour periods on weekdays and
three (3) specific one-hour periods on weekends, selected by the tenant from among
choices offered by the landlord, during which the landlord will have daily access;
and
(3)
The landlord shall notify the tenant when the rental unit has been leased for the
twelve-month period subsequent to the expiration of the rental agreement.
(d)
If the tenant requests repairs and the landlord enters the rental unit to perform
said repairs within fourteen (14) days of the tenant's initial request, the landlord
shall not be obligated to provide the tenant with advance notice of entry. If the
landlord fails to perform said repairs within fourteen (14) days of the tenant's initial
request, the landlord shall be required to provide the tenant with at least twenty-four
(24) hours' advance notice of entry. The notice shall only be effective for a seven-day
period.
(e)
The landlord may enter the rental unit at any time, without advance notice, in case
of emergency. For purposes of this provision, the term "emergency" shall refer to
a situation wherein access to the rental unit is necessary in order to prevent damage
or destruction to the rental unit, other rental units, or the building, or to the
fixtures, equipment, appliances, furniture or other personal property contained therein,
or in order to protect any person from injury. Nonpayment or delinquent payment of
rent shall not constitute an emergency.
(f)
The landlord or landlord's agents shall enter the rental unit only after knocking
on the door and providing the tenant a reasonable opportunity to answer, shall leave
the premises in as good condition as when entered, shall clean and remove dirt and
debris that result from the performance of maintenance and repairs, shall leave a
note indicating the names of the persons who entered the rental unit and shall lock
the rental unit when leaving.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

legal_sources.article: Sec. 12.5-16. Remedies for abuse of access rights.
legal_sources.text:
(a)
If the tenant refuses to allow lawful access, the landlord may obtain injunctive relief
to compel access or terminate the rental agreement. In either case, the landlord may
recover damages and reasonable attorney's fees.
(b)
If the landlord makes an unlawful entry or a lawful entry in an unreasonable manner
the tenant may obtain injunctive relief to prevent the recurrence of the conduct and
recover an amount equal to not more than two (2) months' rent or the damages sustained,
whichever is greater, and reasonable attorney's fees.
(c)
If the landlord makes a lawful entry to make alterations or improvements that materially
interfere with the tenant's use of the premises or if the landlord makes repeated
demands for entry otherwise lawful, but which have the effect of harassing the tenant
after being notified in writing by the tenant that tenant feels harassed by such repeated
demands, the tenant may obtain injunctive relief to prevent the recurrence of the
conduct, or terminate the rental agreement. In each case, the tenant may recover an
amount equal to not more than two (2) months' rent or the damages sustained, whichever
is greater, and reasonable attorney's fees. The provisions of this section shall not
apply to alterations or improvements done by the landlord to correct cited housing
code violations, except in the cases of the landlord's unreasonableness, neglect,
or negligence in correcting the violations.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

legal_sources.text:
(a)
The landlord shall maintain the premises in compliance with all applicable housing
codes of the city and shall promptly make any and all necessary repairs to fulfill
that obligation, provided, however, that the tenant may knowingly and intentionally
elect and agree to repair the premises to bring them into conformity with the applicable
housing codes of the city. The burden shall be on the landlord to establish a knowing
and intentional election on the part of the tenant to repair the premises in compliance
with the applicable housing code. A mere recital in a form lease that tenant has covenanted
to repair will not be sufficient, it being the intention of this article that any
agreement with the tenant to repair be bargained for in fact. A separate hand-written
paragraph in the lease showing:
(1)
That the tenant has been informed of this article and the existing code violations;
(2)
That he/she has affirmatively elected and bargained to repair the violations listed
and other items listed; and
(3)
The inducement for such arrangements, will be prima facie evidence that such provision
was entered into in good faith and was bargained for in fact.
(b)
Nothing in this article shall be interpreted so as to restrict the authority of city
inspectors to cite a landlord for violation of building code provisions.
(c)
Before a tenant initially enters into or renews a rental agreement for a rental unit,
the landlord or any person authorized to enter into a rental agreement on the landlord's
behalf shall disclose to the tenant in writing any housing code violations which have
been cited by the building official and which remain uncorrected for that rental unit
and the common area of the premises.
(d)
This article shall not be interpreted as decreasing or diminishing the implied warranty
of habitability as adopted by the Illinois Supreme Court.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

(a)
A landlord who receives a security deposit of one hundred dollars ($100.00) or more
from a tenant to secure the payment of rent or to compensate for damage to property

legal_sources.text:
(a)
A lessor of residential real property who has received a security deposit from a lessee
to secure the payment of rent or to compensate for damage to the leased property may
not withhold any part of that deposit as compensation for property damage unless he
or she has, within thirty (30) days of the date that the lessee vacated the premises,
furnished to the lessee, delivered in person or by mail directed to his or her last
known address, an itemized statement of the damage allegedly caused to the premises
and the estimated or actual cost for repairing or replacing each item on that statement,
attaching the paid receipts, or copies thereof, for the repair or replacement. If
the lessor utilizes his or her own labor to repair any damage caused by the lessee,
the lessor may include the reasonable cost of his or her labor to repair such damage.
If estimated cost is given, the lessor shall furnish the lessee with paid receipts,
or copies thereof, within thirty (30) days from the date the statement showing estimated
cost was furnished to the lessee, as required by this section. If no such statement
and receipts, or copies thereof, are furnished to the lessee as required by this section,
the lessor shall return the security deposit in full within forty-five (45) days of
the date that the lessee vacated the premises.
(b)
Upon a finding by a circuit court that the landlord has refused to supply the itemized
statement required herein, or has supplied such statement in bad faith, and has failed
or refused to return the amount of the security deposit due within the time limits
provided, the landlord shall be liable for an amount equal to twice the amount of
the security deposit due, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
(c)
Reserved.
(d)
The decorating of the rental unit after the tenant vacates, including painting and
carpet cleaning, unless walls or carpets are damaged beyond normal wear, shall not
be considered as damage and the costs thereof shall not be charged to the security
deposit.

legal_sources.article: Sec. 12.5-23. Tenant remedies for landlord's failure to maintain.
legal_sources.text:
(a)
If the landlord fails to disclose to the tenant in writing any cited housing code
violations as required in this article, or to correct any condition constituting a
subsequently cited housing code violation within the time specified in a duly served
notice to correct such cited housing code violation by the building official, the
tenant affected by the condition may notify the landlord in writing of the tenant's
intention to correct the condition at the landlord's expense. If the landlord, after
receipt of such notice by the tenant, fails to correct the condition within the time
specified for the performance of any act required by the notice of the building official
or any duly granted extension thereof, the tenant, after first obtaining a contractor's
firm certificate of insurance from the qualified appropriate tradesman who is to perform
the work, and after furnishing such certificate to the landlord in the case of any
work to be done on the premises, may have the work done in a competent manner and,
after submitting to the landlord a paid itemized invoice and, where applicable, a
properly completed waiver of lien, may deduct from his or her rent the amount thereof.
(b)
If the cited housing code violation is one involving essential services which a landlord
fails to supply contrary to the rental agreement, or if such violation is one giving
rise to a hazardous condition which materially and immediately affects health and
safety, the tenant affected by the condition may, in the alternative to the remedy
set forth above, after the city's deadline for compliance has passed, notify the landlord
in writing of the tenant's intention to:
(1)
Procure reasonable amounts of heat, hot water, running water, electricity, gas or
other essential service during the period of the landlord's noncompliance and deduct
their cost from the rent; or
(2)
Procure substitute housing during the period of the landlord's noncompliance, in which
case the tenant is excused from paying rent for the period of the landlord's noncompliance.
The tenant's actual cost of substitute housing may be deducted from the rent, provided
that the amount deducted shall not exceed the average cost for a hotel/motel room
in Urbana.
(c)
If the landlord fails to provide essential services or to correct the hazardous condition
within the time specified in the notice to correct the cited housing code violation
or any extension granted by the building official, or if any such similar uncorrected
condition or uncorrected interruption of services for any significant period recurs
and is cited by the city more than three (3) times in any twelve-month period, the
tenant may vacate the premises and terminate the rental agreement, in which case the
tenant may recover from the landlord all rent payments not applied to rent accrued
prior to the termination of the rental agreement and all damage or security deposits
not rightfully applied to damages to the rental unit.
(d)
The provisions of this section may not be used by the tenant more than three (3) times
during any twelve-month period nor may the combined total dollar amount so deducted
or excused during any such period exceed two (2) months' rent. If the tenant proceeds
under this section, the tenant may not proceed under any other sections for such breach.
(e)
The tenant may not exercise his or her rights under this section if the condition
was caused by the inability or unwillingness of a utility supplier to provide service
or by the deliberate or negligent act or omission of the tenant, a member of his or
her family, or other person on the premises with the tenant's consent.
(Ord. No. 9394-58, § 1, 1-18-94)

legal_sources.text:
Sec. 1. Statement of damage.
(a) Except as provided in subsection (b), a lessor of residential real property
who has received a security deposit from a lessee to secure the payment
of rent or to compensate for damage to the leased premises may not
withhold any part of that deposit as reimbursement for property damage
unless the lessor has, within 30 days of the date that the lessee vacated the
leased premises or within 30 days of the date the lessee's right of possession ends, whichever is later, furnished to the lessee, by personal delivery, by postmarked mail
directed to his or her last known address, or by electronic mail to a verified electronic mail address provided by the lessee, an itemized statement of the damage
allegedly caused to the leased premises and the estimated or actual cost for
repairing or replacing each item on that statement, attaching the paid
receipts, or copies thereof, for the repair or replacement.
If the lessor utilizes his or her own labor to repair or replace any damage or damaged items caused
by the lessee, the lessor may include the reasonable cost of his or her
labor to repair or replace such damage or damaged items. If estimated
cost is given, the lessor shall furnish to the lessee, delivered in person or by postmarked mail directed to the last known address of the lessee or another address provided by the lessee, paid receipts,
or copies thereof, within 30 days from the date the statement showing
estimated cost was furnished to the lessee, as required by this Section. If a written lease specifies the cost for cleaning, repair, or replacement of any component of the leased premises or any component of the building or common areas that, if damaged, will not be replaced, the lessor may withhold the dollar amount specified in the lease. Costs specified in a written lease shall be for damage beyond normal wear and tear and reasonable to restore the leased premises to the same condition as at the time the lease began. The itemized statement shall reference the dollar amount specified in the written lease associated with the specific building component or amenity and include a copy of the applicable portion of the lease. Deductions for costs or values not specified in the lease shall otherwise comply with the requirements of this Section.
If no such statement and receipts, or copies thereof, are furnished to
the lessee as required by this Section, the lessor shall return the
security deposit in full within 45 days of the date that the lessee vacated
the premises, delivered in person or by postmarked mail directed to the last known address of the lessee or another address provided by the lessee. If the lessee fails to provide the lessor with a mailing address or electronic mail address, the lessor shall not be held liable for any damages or penalties as a result of the lessee's failure to provide an address.
(b) If, through no fault of the lessor, the lessor is unable to produce as required in subsection (a) receipts for repairs or replacements, or copies thereof, then the lessor shall produce an itemized list of the cost of repair or replacement, any other evidence the lessor has of the cost, and a verified statement of the lessor or the agent of the lessor detailing the specific reasons why the lessor is unable to produce the required receipts or copies and verifying that the lessor has provided all other evidence the lessor has of the cost.
(c) Upon a finding by a circuit court that a lessor has refused to supply
the itemized statement required by this Section, or has supplied such statement
in bad faith, and has failed or refused to return the amount of the security
deposit due within the time limits provided, the lessor shall be liable
for an amount equal to twice the amount of the security deposit due, together
with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

legal_sources.law: Residential Tenants' Right to Repair Act
legal_sources.text:
Sec. 5. Repair; deduction from rent. If a repair is required under a
residential lease
agreement or required under a law, administrative rule, or local ordinance or
regulation,
and the reasonable cost of the repair does not exceed the lesser of $500 or
one-half of the
monthly rent, the tenant may notify the landlord in writing by registered or certified mail or other restricted delivery service to the address of the landlord or an agent of the landlord as indicated on the lease agreement; if an address is not listed, the tenant may send notice to the landlord's last known address of the tenant's
intention to
have the repair made at the landlord's expense.
If the landlord fails to make the repair
within 14 days after being notified by the tenant as provided above or more promptly
as
conditions require in the case of an emergency, the tenant may have the repair
made in
a
workmanlike manner and in compliance with the appropriate law, administrative
rule, or
local ordinance or regulation. Emergencies include conditions that will cause irreparable harm to the apartment or any fixture attached to the apartment if not immediately repaired or any condition that poses an immediate threat to the health or safety of any occupant of the dwelling or any common area. After submitting to the landlord a paid bill
from an
appropriate tradesman or supplier unrelated to the tenant, the tenant may deduct from his or
her rent the
amount of the bill, not to exceed the limits specified by this Section and not
to exceed the
reasonable price then customarily charged for the repair. If not clearly indicated on the bill submitted by the tenant, the tenant shall also provide to the landlord in writing, at the time of the submission of the bill, the name, address, and telephone number for the tradesman or supplier that provided the repair services. A tenant may not
repair at the
landlord's expense if the condition was caused by the deliberate or negligent
act or
omission of the tenant, a member of the tenant's family, or another person on
the
premises with the tenant's consent.
legal_sources.applicability: Written restricted-delivery notice, cure period, cost cap, qualified repair and fault conditions apply; read with Secs. 10 and 15.

legal_sources.law: Residential Tenants' Right to Repair Act
legal_sources.text:
Sec. 15. Tenant liabilities and responsibilities. The tenant is responsible for ensuring that:
(1) the repairs are performed in a workmanlike manner
in compliance with the appropriate law, administrative rule, or local ordinance or regulation;
(2) the tradesman or supplier that is hired by the
tenant to perform the repairs holds the appropriate valid license or certificate required by State or municipal law to make the repair; and
(3) the tradesman or supplier is adequately insured
to cover any bodily harm or property damage that is caused by the negligence or substandard performance of the repairs by the tradesman or supplier.
The tenant is responsible for any damages to the premises caused by a tradesman or supplier hired by the tenant. A tenant shall not be entitled to exercise the remedies provided for in this Act if the tenant does not comply with the requirements of this Section.
legal_sources.applicability: Repair-and-deduct requires appropriate licensing, insurance and workmanship; tenant may be liable for contractor damage.

Sec. 9-213.1.
Duty of landlord to mitigate damages.
After January
1, 1984, a
landlord or his or her agent shall take reasonable measures to mitigate the damages
recoverable against a defaulting lessee.
legal_sources.applicability: Reasonable mitigation of recoverable damages against a defaulting lessee; not automatic cancellation of every agreed early-termination charge.

legal_sources.law: Residential Lead-Based Paint Hazard Reduction Act
legal_sources.text:
(27)  Target housing
The term “target housing” means any housing constructed prior to 1978, except housing for the elderly or persons with disabilities or any 0-bedroom dwelling (unless any child who is less than 6 years of age resides or is expected to reside in such housing). In the case of jurisdictions which banned the sale or use of lead-based paint prior to 1978, the Secretary, at the Secretary’s discretion, may designate an earlier date.
legal_sources.source_version: OLRC text through Public Law 119-124 (2026-10-15)
legal_sources.applicability: Definition of target housing; construction before 1978 and the enumerated exceptions must be established, not inferred from a missing clause.

legal_sources.law: Residential Lead-Based Paint Hazard Reduction Act
legal_sources.text:
(1)  Lead-based paint hazards
Not later than 2 years after October 28, 1992, the Secretary and the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency shall promulgate regulations under this section for the disclosure of lead-based paint hazards in target housing which is offered for sale or lease. The regulations shall require that, before the purchaser or lessee is obligated under any contract to purchase or lease the housing, the seller or lessor shall⁠—
(A)  provide the purchaser or lessee with a lead hazard information pamphlet, as prescribed by the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency under section 406 of the Toxic Substances Control Act [15 U.S.C. 2686];
(B)  disclose to the purchaser or lessee the presence of any known lead-based paint, or any known lead-based paint hazards, in such housing and provide to the purchaser or lessee any lead hazard evaluation report available to the seller or lessor; and
(C)  permit the purchaser a 10-day period (unless the parties mutually agree upon a different period of time) to conduct a risk assessment or inspection for the presence of lead-based paint hazards.
legal_sources.source_version: OLRC text through Public Law 119-124 (2026-10-15)
legal_sources.applicability: Target-housing disclosure framework; the ten-day inspection language is for a purchaser, not a universal tenant inspection period. Check implementing-rule exceptions separately.

result.summary: 合同文本极短，仅说明出租方将住宅出租给承租方、房屋使用 Urbana 邮寄地址，并附有一项“边界记录”称该住宅位于 Urbana 市界之外。该边界记录属于合同所载事实，但未提供来源或核实材料；因此不能据此断言 Urbana 第 12.5 章必然不适用，也不能断言必然适用。合同未写明租金、租期、押金、维修、进入、续租、驱逐、费用、铅漆披露等条款，这些均需向出租方核实。
